title_en: Notice of the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on Forwarding the Notice of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce on Issues Concerning the Handling of Individual, Partnership, and Private Enterprises Holding Business Licenses for Collective Enterprises
full_text_en:
General Office of the Supreme People's Court

Forwarding the Notice of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce

on Handling the Issue of Individual, Partnership, and Private Enterprises

Holding Business Licenses of Collectively-Owned Enterprises

Fa Ban [1987] No. 69

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government:

We hereby forward to you the Notice of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce on Handling the Issue of Individual, Partnership, and Private Enterprises Holding Business Licenses of Collectively-Owned Enterprises, for reference in trial work.

Appendix: Notice on Handling the Issue of Individual, Partnership, and Private Enterprises Holding Business Licenses of Collectively-Owned Enterprises

December 18, 1987

State Administration for Industry and Commerce

Notice on Handling the Issue of Individual, Partnership, and Private Enterprises

Holding Business Licenses of Collectively-Owned Enterprises

Gong Shang Ge Zi [1987] No. 319

To the Administrations for Industry and Commerce of all provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities directly under the Central Government, cities with independent planning status (districts), and Nanjing and Chengdu:

In recent years, in some localities, the examination during enterprise registration has not been strict enough, resulting in the identification of certain industrial and commercial businesses individually invested, family-invested, or partnership-invested and privately operated as collectively-owned enterprises. Some industrial and commercial businesses invested by private individuals, which were registered in the name of subordinate enterprises of state-owned or collectively-owned units, have also been identified as collectively-owned enterprises. Furthermore, some individual industrial and commercial households and privately operated enterprises that have attached themselves to collectively-owned enterprises have also been identified as collectively-owned enterprises. The business licenses held by these enterprises fail to accurately reflect the nature of ownership of the enterprises, causing difficulties for judicial authorities in handling certain criminal cases and economic dispute cases, and also causing undue political impact and economic losses to the parties concerned.

In order to resolve the above issues, the following notice is hereby issued:

1. For enterprises that hold business licenses of collectively-owned enterprises but are in reality individually operated, partnership-operated, or privately operated, the administrative authorities for industry and commerce shall make corrections in accordance with the relevant provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, the Interim Regulations on the Administration of Urban and Rural Individual Industrial and Commercial Households, and the Notice of this Administration on Printing and Distributing the Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Interim Regulations on the Administration of Urban and Rural Individual Industrial and Commercial Households, among others. When a judicial authority is hearing a criminal case or an economic dispute case involving the issue of the nature of an enterprise, the administrative authority for industry and commerce may, in the spirit of seeking truth from facts, provide information to the judicial authority and suggest that the nature of ownership be treated according to what it actually is.

2. In accordance with the provisions of the Notice of this Administration on Using New Business Licenses (Gong Shang Qi Zi [1987] No. 257), after the administrative authorities for industry and commerce at all levels begin to issue new business licenses on January 1, 1988, no business license of a collectively-owned enterprise shall be issued to industrial and commercial businesses that are individually invested, family-invested, or partnership-invested. No relevant unit may apply for registration of a private investor as a collectively-owned enterprise in a collective name, nor shall any private operator who has found an attached unit on its own apply for registration as a collectively-owned enterprise and obtain a business license.

3. The business license is a certificate issued by the administrative authority for industry and commerce, authorized by the State, to enterprises, individual industrial and commercial households, and other business entities to obtain lawful business rights, and is also an important basis for judicial authorities in handling relevant cases. When accepting and processing registrations, the administrative authorities for industry and commerce shall, in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations of the State, carefully examine and strictly control the applications, fill in the registration items as required, and shall not be subject to interference by any unit or individual. Henceforth, if any inconsistency between the economic component and the actual situation again occurs in the issuance of business licenses, the person directly responsible shall bear the corresponding responsibility.

December 11, 1987
